title: Add RAG developer primer and local tooling slate
author: Priya Patel
description:
Motivation: onboarding engineers to RAG workflows often stalls on two fronts: (1) lack of a compact, opinionated developer primer that ties prompt templates, tool contracts, and evaluation checks together; (2) no single local toolkit to iterate on tool stubs and a lightweight playground for manual QA. This PR adds a short, example-driven Developer Primer, a small local tooling slate (Node CLI + Python connectors), and a static playground that can run in devcontainers. The goal is fast onboarding loops for teams trialing RAG patterns with Redwood SDKs and for contributors who want runnable examples before deploying to production.

Changes included (high-level):
- docs/dev-primer/DEVELOPER_PRIMER.md: new 7-section primer with recommended prompt contracts, structured-output patterns, and an evaluation checklist.
- examples/local-tooling/cli/: a tiny Node-based CLI (ts) that scaffolds tool contracts, runs a mock indexer, and spins up the playground server.
- examples/local-tooling/connectors/python_sample.py: minimal Python connector demonstrating streaming chunked uploads to a local indexer and sample retrieval policy.
- playground/static/: a single-file static playground (vanilla JS) that demonstrates tool-calling UI and replayable step traces.
- examples/indexer/mapping.yaml: compact mapping for incremental indexing used by the included mock indexer.
- docs/site-nav.yml: docs site TOC entry to surface the primer under "Quickstarts & Examples".
- .github/workflows/examples-smoke.yml: small CI job to run the playground smoke test and examples lint.

Checklist: 
- [x] Developer primer draft and screenshots
- [x] Minimal CLI + scaffolding for tool contracts
- [x] Lightweight playground and replay traces
- [x] Smoke CI that runs in ~4 minutes
- [x] Unit tests for connector example (basic assertions)
- [x] Docs site navigation updated

Commits summary:
- feat(primer): add developer primer with stepwise walkthroughs and checklists
- feat(cli): add ts CLI scaffold to generate tool contract stubs and start playground
- feat(playground): add static playground UI and replay fixture runner
- chore(ci): add examples-smoke workflow and example runner scripts
- fix(tests): adjust connector test timing to avoid flaky sleeps

Why this is different: unlike larger quickstarts that target full cloud deployment, this PR emphasizes local-first iteration: reproducible small steps, explicit structured-output contracts, and a devloop that exercises the same contract surfaces the production runtime will use. It should reduce onboarding time and lower friction for contributions that add new tool adapters.

Related: ENG-2145 (reduce onboarding friction), PM-732 (developer docs sprint).
